messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a regression on the MoE multi-GPU runs (64G dedicated). ~20% token latency increase for long-context traces (>1024). Attached profiler snapshot below, but top-level: all-to-all spikes around step boundaries and extra matmul CPU fallback during routing hotpath. :thinking:

kevin: Oof. Did this start after the kernel-table reorder change last week? My gut: kernel selection could be choosing a slower kernel for the small/medium dims we hit during routing. Any flamegraphs?

maya: Paste from perf trace (condensed):
```
flame: all_to_all (50ms spikes) -> nccl_alltoall (avg 3ms, spike 48ms)
cpu: kernel_selector::choose() -> fallback_matmul_fp32 (12ms)
gpu: kv_cache_miss_handler -> double_write -> extra allreduce
```

arnav: I reproduced locally with a synthetic mix: `scripts/repro/all2all_hotspot.py --batch 48 --seq 1536 --moe 8 --skew 0.42`. When skew>0.3 we see the same waveform. Also noticed kernel selector now prefers the new fused GEMM for dim<2048, but that fused path does more shared memory syncs on small workloads.

lisa: KV cache telemetry shows "invalidation_count" jumped 3x in the same window. Looks like when expert swap occurs and we reroute, some keys are re-indexed causing prefetch to miss -> causes recompute + extra reduce.

perf-bot: [CI perf-run] mocha/canary-moe: latency +18% vs baseline (2026-03-01). Repro script and raw trace attached to the CI run.

kevin: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) kernel selector fallback order causes hitting slower fused kernel on skewed batches; (2) KV cache thrash due to routing-group churn causing duplicate all-to-all payloads. Both would amplify nccl overhead.

maya: Proposed quick mitigations: rollback kernel-table for dims < 1024 for canary, add a routing pre-shuffle to smooth expert skew, and add a KV-prefetch warmup window for the first 2 tokens after a swap. Also change batching heuristic to prefer size-sorted batching for MoE routes so per-shard dims are steadier.

arnav: For the kernel side, we can add an A/B flag in runtime: `kernel_policy=stable|new`. If stable is selected for <512/1024 we'll force the old matmul path. I can patch a microbenchmark to compare throughput+latency across dim ranges.

lisa: I'll queue canary runs: (a) kernel rollback, (b) kv-prefetch warmup, (c) routing pre-shuffle. Running on `dedicated-stg-12` — ETA ~1h per experiment. I'll post raw traces as they finish.

kevin: Also want to test changing NCCL algorithm (ring vs tree) for these all-to-all shapes; ring seems to spike more when payloads are imbalanced. Add a perf test: `nv-nccl-test --pattern=alltoall --algo=tree --msgsize=8KB` and compare.

maya: Good call. If tree reduces tail spikes we should add a runtime knob to prefer tree for MoE routing. Also, add tracepoints around `router->shuffle()` and `kv_cache->lookup()` so we can measure overlap: comm start vs compute start. Current traces suggest poor comm/compute overlap.

perf-bot: Perf test queued: `moe_canary_kv_warmup_rollout` (job #4821).

arnav: FYI: I found one low-level issue — when routing group size variation exceeds threshold, we serialize an expert enqueue path to avoid OOM; that serialization is fighting with async allreduce and causing the alltoall peak. Fix would be to allow bounded parallel enqueues + backpressure instead of global serialize. I'll prototype.

lisa: Canary 1 done (kernel rollback) — preliminary: tail latency down ~12%, avg down ~8%. Leaving canary running for longer.

maya: Nice. Keep me posted. If rollback holds, we'll ship rollback to prod-dedicated and then iterate on longer-term fixes (routing smoothing + kv prefetch + enqueue parallelism). Filing follow-up ticket: ENG-RT-4123. Don't escalate to incidents channel yet — it's a perf regression but not a customer-facing outage. :+1:

kevin: Thanks all. Assigning myself to run NCCL tree vs ring sweep and evaluating async-allreduce options.

arnav: I'll send the microbench numbers and a proposed patch for bounded enqueue later today.

lisa: Adding traces to the ticket. If anyone wants the raw canary logs, ping me and I’ll share the link. :mag_right:
